---
title: "Before the day"
---
The day is worked in R, inside an IDE, on a ready-made workspace that the setup page prepares. The browser lab holds the same exercise in a browser tab: it is what the facilitator drives on the shared screen and the place to carry on if a machine fails, and it reaches the same numbers.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Setup](../../setup.qmd) | Install R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the workspace zip and run `R/check_setup.R` until it prints OK. Open the browser lab once as well and confirm that it loads on the machine you will use. The [help page](../../help.qmd) has the problems other participants have met. | 30 to 60 minutes, once |
| [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](../../companion/ide.qmd) | Optional. Where the console, the variables and the data viewer are in the IDE you chose, and what changes between the three. Section 6 is a six-step run through the workspace. | 30 minutes |
| [Exercise overview](../../exercise/index.qmd) | Read the claim you will be working on and the table of what the five Multi100 analysts found when they reanalysed it. | 10 minutes |
| [Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd) | Optional. Worth the time if you have never written R: objects, data frames, reading a CSV, and the pipe. | An evening |
| [Reading a specification curve](../../exercise/reading-inference.qmd) | Optional pre-reading for Part 4, on what a large set of results together can and cannot establish. | 20 minutes |

**By the start of the day** you have the workspace working on the machine you will use, and you know what the claim is and how far apart the five Multi100 analysts landed on it.
